executableEdges.reason: Think calls the agent's tools and hooks, and the Worker calls the object's RPC methods, as Promise-returning methods. `runInterviewEffect` runs one program from interview.ts (an Effect over the object's SQLite and workspace) per call; all interview logic is in those programs and in shared/machine.ts.

hostTooling.reason: Host programs on the operator's machine: the end-to-end player (play.mjs, spends model tokens), local D1 migration, the cf token preflight, hook and compiler installers.
The customer's page: DOM event wiring and fetches against the Worker's /api. It is not Effect code and never runs on the Worker; it only imports the pure shared modules.
The vite-plus config runs in the build host; it reads process.env.VITEST only to skip the Cloudflare plugin for plain unit tests.

allowedAdapters.reason: The fetch edge hands /i/* and /admin/* to one Effect web handler per request and copies its response into a native Response; Durable Object calls are wrapped as effects (`rpc`). No business logic lives here beyond routing.
The framework's Promise contract: tool executes and hooks return the promise of one Effect program; no `async` and no business logic lives in the class.

aiProviderTransports.reason: The model is reached through Think's AI SDK contract (getModel returns an AI SDK LanguageModel; DeepSeek via @ai-sdk/openai-compatible), which is the framework's own boundary; there is no Effect AI client in the loop.
